newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin makes first TV appearance in three weeks.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin makes first TV appearance in three weeks.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin appeared on television on Tuesday for the first time in three weeks, gesticulating as he chatted with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and smiling broadly as he spoke to the secretary of the Commonwealth of Independent States.

The president, who is recovering from pneumonia, has clearly lost weight since he fell ill, but he looked relaxed during two brief film clips. There was no soundtrack and it was not clear exactly what was being discussed.
Aides said Yeltsin, who turns 66 on Saturday, visited the Kremlin on Tuesday for the second time since he left hospital to meet Chernomyrdin and CIS secretary Ivan Korotchenya.
Presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin had spent three hours in the Kremlin before returning to the state residence outside Moscow where he is recovering.
Yeltsin's political opponents have questioned the president's ability to rule Russia and have discussed trying to remove him for health reasons.
The president also went to the Kremlin on January 22. That visit was not shown on television and it failed to dampen speculation about Yeltsin's ability to rule.

Yeltsin, acting on doctors' orders, on Monday cancelled a planned trip to the Netherlands to meet senior European officials. But aides say French President Jacques Chirac will visit Moscow as planned on Sunday.
